newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard Smith sees better year result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard Smith sees better year result.

text.p: Shipping, engineering and hardware group Howard Smith Ltd said on Tuesday that full-year earnings were expected to show an improvement on last year's results.

"The managing director, Dr Ken Moss, said the outlook for the second half remained positive with full year earnings expected to be better than last year's results," the company said in a statement accompanying its half-year results.
Operating profit after tax for the half-year rose 56.8 percent to A$61.3 million.
The company announced a fully franked interim dividend of 17 cents per share payable on April 4.
Moss said the half-year result was a very strong vindication of the company's focus on growth, particularly given the downturn in the Australian housing market.
"Profits in the second half of the year are expected to at least match profits earned in the first half, underpinned by continued growth in sales from Hardwarehouse stores," the company said.
"The anticipated recovery in the Australian housing market is not expected to significantly influence second half sales," it added.
"BBC Hardware recorded an impressive 3.5 percent increase in sales on the previous corresponding half year," Moss said.
"Retail sales were up very strongly by 12 percent, mainly because of the expansion of our Hardware house chain of stores which have high customer acceptance."
Moss said that although trade sales remained slow, the growth of the Hardwarehouse chain and improvement in retail sales had helped increase net sales margins to six percent from 5.8 percent.
The company's industrial supplies distributor, Blackwoods, reported a three percent increase in sales, in a difficult market.

The Engineering Division, operating through A Goninan & Co Ltd, produced a 47 percent increase in revenue, brought about by the delivery of the first 20 of 120 locomotives to National Rail Corporation and progress on other major rolling stock contracts in New South Wales and Queensland.
The National Rail Corporation locomotive order would make a continuing strong contribution to Goninan second half earnings.
Moss said the company's Marine Division had made a smooth withdrawal from shipping, with the sale of the tanker Canopus contributing most of the abnormal profit of $14.4 million.
Goninan had won new contracts, including 200 coal wagons for Queensland Rail, worth $16 million, and its second half earnings were expected to be above its first half contribution.
The marine division's towage interests in Australia and United Kingdom had contributed significantly to the Group's improved profit performance, he said.
Moss said Howard Smith's gearing had reduced to 44 percent at December 31 from 60 percent at June 30, 1996.
